ORDER This first application has been filed by applicant under section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No.29 of 2011 registered at Police Station Inderganj, District Gwalior (M.P.), for offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 506 of IPC,
Section 3/6 of the Madhya Pradesh Nikshepakon Ke Hiton Ka Sanrakshan Adhiniyam, 2000 and enhanced Sections 45S/ 1A, 45S/58B, (5-A) of the RBI Act, 1934 and Sections 4, 5, 6 of the Money Circulation Scheme Act.

sentences.text: The applicant is in judicial custody since 10-02-2024.

A s per the prosecution case, Dipak Chandwani submitted a written complaint against the applicant and other co-accused that he and his friends and family members deposited certain amounts with G.N. Dairies, G.N. Gold Ltd. and Navnidhi Commodities Ltd in year 2003.
The concerned company issued polices in their favour but despite maturity of polices, no payment has been made.
The applicant and other co-accused have cheated and misappropriated the money deposited by them.

After enquiry into the complaint, for offence 2 MCRC-24592-2024 punishable under Sections 420,
467, 468, 506 of IPC, Section 3/6 of the Madhya Pradesh Nikshepakon Ke Hiton Ka Sanrakshan Adhiniyam, 2000 at PS Inderganj, District Gwalior.

sentences.text: Applicant was arrested on 10-02-2024.
He is in custody ever since.

Thereafter, prosecution for offence punishable under Sections 45S/ 1A, 45S/58B,
(5-A) of the RBI Act, 1934 and Sections 4, 5, 6 of the Money Circulation Scheme Act was added.
On completion of investigation, Final Report against applicant has been submitted on 09-05-2024.
Learned Counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, submits that applicant is falsely implicated in the matter.
Learned counsel further submits that applicant has already been resigned from the post of Director of G.N. Dairies Ltd. and G.N. Gold in year 2009.

sentences.text: Referring to Form No.32 under Sections 303, 264 and 266 of the Companies Act, learned counsel contends that Coordinate Bench of this Court have taken cognizance of resignation of the applicant in year 2009 and extended him benefit of bail in other criminal matters registered on identical allegations.
Learned counsel further submits that applicant is aged around 55 years and he is in custody since 2016 in other matters.
He is formally arrested in this matter on 10-02-2024.
There is no likelihood of tampering with the evidence by the applicant.
There is no likelihood of his absconsion leaving his family and home.
Jail incarceration is causing financial hardship to the family of applicant.
Trial would take time to complete.
Therefore, applicant may be extended the benefit of bail.
Per contra, learned Counsel for the State opposes the bail application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence and cites criminal history of 11cases of similar nature against the applicant.
In reply, learned Counsel for the applicant submits that all the matters relate to identical allegations.
Applicant stands acquitted in five cases.
Other 3 MCRC-24592-2024 matters are pending for trial.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
Considering the arguments advanced by both the parties and overall circumstances of the case but without commenting on merits of the case, this Court is inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Thus, the application is allowed.
